data.narrative:
Terrestrial Energy operates in the nuclear energy sector at the public stage, having raised $280M to date. The valuation universe consists of 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private competitors (Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, NuScale Power), though the sector remains concentrated with limited comparable companies.

The peer-median method is not applicable here. The nuclear energy sector contains only 4 same-stage companies total, with insufficient depth at adjacent stages or similar valuation tiers to establish a reliable median. A narrow peer comparison would require at least 3 datapoints within filtered criteria; the available set does not meet this threshold. Applying an all-sector median would introduce distortion given the heterogeneity in business models, technology readiness, and capital requirements across nuclear subsegments.

Without a sufficient peer cohort, valuation triangulation via traditional comparable-company analysis cannot be reliably executed. This analysis would benefit from alternative methods—such as DCF modeling incorporating technology development milestones, regulatory pathway analysis, or precedent transaction data from the nuclear sector—to establish a defensible range. The key uncertainty remains the scarcity of direct comparables at Terrestrial Energy's stage and technology focus, limiting the precision of public-market benchmarking approaches.
